CanonicalVars.issue: `new BlockVar(13m, ValueProp.Move)` maps to `_block = 13`, but the second var `new DynamicVar("Equilibrium", 1m)` (Equilibrium.cs:19-23) has no `_`-attribute -- the sim passes the literal 1. `base_block` is right; `magic_number` returns None where the game prints a second var. The BlockVar is Move WITHOUT Unpowered -> POWERED block, so this card is NOT in gap G1's blast radius. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the applied number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.rationale: Order matches: `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Block, cardPlay)` FIRST (Equilibrium.cs:34) == `BlockCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._block, card=self)`, then `PowerCmd.Apply<RetainHandPower>(..., DynamicVars["Equilibrium"].BaseValue, ...)` (35) == `PowerCmd.apply(..., RetainHandPower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`. Presentation, folded in: the Retain hover tip (25).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Block.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` (Equilibrium.cs:40) == `self._block += 3` (13 -> 16). The RetainHandPower amount stays 1 when upgraded on both sides -- upgraded values checked.
